definitions.definition: Ttor = reals/(2*pi*integers), with normalized measure dx/(2*pi); spatial products and integrals are on this domain.
For an integrable periodic f, Fourier(f)(k)=hat f(k)=(2*pi)^(-1) integral_0^(2*pi) f(x) exp(-i*k*x) dx; the transform extends to distributions by duality.

For every real s, H^s(Ttor) is the completion of trigonometric polynomials with ||f||_(H^s)^2=sum_(k in Z) <k>^(2*s)|hat f(k)|^2, <k>=(1+k^2)^(1/2). Negative spaces are interpreted as distributions. Homogeneous norms on zero-mean distributions are ||f||_(dot H^s)^2=sum_(k!=0)|k|^(2*s)|hat f(k)|^2. Real means hat f(-k)=conjugate(hat f(k)); mean zero means hat f(0)=0.

L2=H^0(Ttor), with ||f||_2^2=(2*pi)^(-1) integral |f|^2 dx. More generally L^p uses the same normalized measure; L^infinity is essential supremum. Sequence ell^2 uses counting measure on Z (or Z\{0} when specified). Time suprema use continuous representatives; derivative norms are essential suprema.

definitions.definition: P0(f)=hat f(0), identified with a constant function.
Pnz=I-P0, denoted P in the supplied proof. Fourier projections P_leq(N) and P_gt(N) retain |k|<=N and |k|>N respectively, for N>=0.
Dinv=partial_x^(-1) has Fourier multiplier (i*k)^(-1) at nonzero integer k and zero at k=0. Dinv2=(Dinv)^2 is denoted D^(-2).
Bop_t(f,g)=S_(-t)*partial_x[(S_t f)(S_t g)], initially for smooth periodic functions and by distributional product for L2 inputs.

For a grid start t_n=n*tau, tau>0, and time-independent mean-zero w, Stage_n(t;w)=(1/2) integral_(t_n)^t Bop_s(w,w) ds for t in [t_n,t_n+tau]. The associated bilinear stage has w1,w2 in its two slots.
For 0<gamma<=1, agamma=1/2-gamma if gamma<1/2, agamma=1/8 if gamma=1/2, and agamma=0 if gamma>1/2.

inputs.statement: Let 0<sigma_s<=1, tau_s>0, t_j=j*tau_s>=0 and t in [t_j,t_j+tau_s]. For time-independent mean-zero g1,g2 in Hsrc^sigma_s define Fsrc_j(t;g1,g2)=(1/2)integral_(t_j)^t exp(s partial_x^3)*partial_x[(exp(-s partial_x^3)g1)(exp(-s partial_x^3)g2)]ds. With beta0=2*sigma_s-3/2 for sigma_s<1/2, beta0=-1/2-epsilon for sigma_s=1/2 (any fixed sufficiently small epsilon>0), and beta0=sigma_s-1 for sigma_s>1/2, the source gives, for beta in [beta0,1+sigma_s], ||Fsrc_j(t;g1,g2)||_(Hsrc^beta)<=C*tau_s^((1+sigma_s-beta)/(1+sigma_s-beta0))*||g1||_(Hsrc^sigma_s)*||g2||_(Hsrc^sigma_s), with C depending only on exponents (and epsilon) and uniform in j,tau_s,t and support. Its endpoint formula is (1/6)[S_(-s) Pnz((S_s Dinv g1)(S_s Dinv g2))]_(s=t_j)^(s=t).

argument.text: H002 gives 0<gamma<=1. In E004 set sigma_s=gamma and at gamma=1/2 choose epsilon=1/8. Its a(sigma_s) is exactly agamma. Source norms are sqrt(2*pi) times ours; dividing the product estimate by sqrt(2*pi) changes only its constant. This proves ||fg||_2<=C_gamma||f||_(H^gamma)||g||_(H^agamma) for arbitrary f,g in the displayed spaces.

Take arbitrary 0<tau<=1, n>=0 and mean-zero w with ||w||_(H^gamma)<=M0. E003 with sigma_s=gamma, g1=g2=w and epsilon=1/8 in the middle case estimates our Stage after the same fixed norm conversion. At beta=agamma the exponent theta=(1+gamma-agamma)/(1+gamma-beta0) equals (1/2+2*gamma)/(5/2-gamma) for gamma<1/2, 11/17 for gamma=1/2 and (1+gamma)/2 for gamma>1/2. These are >=gamma: in the first case the numerator minus gamma times denominator is gamma^2-gamma/2+1/2>0; the middle is >1/2; the last follows from gamma<=1. In each case beta0<=agamma<=1+gamma and 0<=agamma<1. Since tau<=1, tau^theta<=tau^gamma. At beta=1+gamma the source exponent is zero. This proves both uniform stage estimates, with constants depending only on gamma,M0.
